entries.test: Public records of the LLMs Marcus had examined by publication and their outputs would show whether each frequently fabricated content.
entries.note: The preceding sentence supplies the assertion that these models fabricate a lot; the scope is models he has seen.

entries.test: Documented classroom incidents and student and teacher reports would show whether high school students enthusiastically adopted Galactica and used it to deceive and intimidate some teachers.
entries.note: This is a firm forecast with no stated deadline.
“The rest of us” does not precisely specify everyone except students who actually use Galactica, as the normalization does. The prescribed emotional response is a value judgment.

entries.test: The shared Galactica outputs, checked against established scientific and mathematical sources, would show whether they presented fabricated or invalid material as factual science and mathematics.
entries.note: “Pitch perfect” is evaluative, but the central assertion about bogus content presented as factual is checkable.
